    index_ops

    pykmhelpers.pipeline.index_ops

    Build and merge k-mer indexes from index definitions or span registries.

    IndexOps is the entry point; the other modules are its components.

    IndexOps

    Plans k-mer index builds against the kmindex registry BUILD_DIR.

    Loads an index definition or a span registry (see sources), plans every selected definition as unregistered kmtricks runs, then the publication of each target: the runs of its parts, merged with its current version when it is already registered, become BUILD_DIR/<target>. A definition that is not a part of a selected merge is its own target. Nothing is built: write_plan() writes the scripts of every task and plan.yaml, which apply runs (runner.PlanRunner).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    config IndexOpsConfig

    Runtime configuration governing paths, build parameters, filtering, and execution behaviour. See IndexOpsConfig.

    		 required

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    config IndexOpsConfig

    The resolved configuration (workdir is made absolute on construction).
    work_dir str

    BUILD_DIR, the kmindex registry.
    asset_dir str

    <work_dir>/assets - one folder of scripts per session.
    log_dir str

    <work_dir>/logs - log file destination.
    timestamp str

    YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS string captured at construction.

    class IndexOps:
    """Plans k-mer index builds against the kmindex registry ``BUILD_DIR``.

    Loads an index definition or a span registry (see ``sources``), plans
    every selected definition as unregistered kmtricks runs, then the
    publication of each target: the runs of its parts, merged with its
    current version when it is already registered, become
    ``BUILD_DIR/<target>``. A definition that is not a part of a selected
    merge is its own target. Nothing is built: ``write_plan()`` writes the
    scripts of every task and ``plan.yaml``, which ``apply`` runs
    (``runner.PlanRunner``).

    Args:
        config: Runtime configuration governing paths, build parameters,
            filtering, and execution behaviour.  See ``IndexOpsConfig``.

    Attributes:
        config (IndexOpsConfig): The resolved configuration (``workdir`` is
            made absolute on construction).
        work_dir (str): ``BUILD_DIR``, the kmindex registry.
        asset_dir (str): ``<work_dir>/assets`` - one folder of scripts per session.
        log_dir (str): ``<work_dir>/logs`` - log file destination.
        timestamp (str): ``YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS`` string captured at construction.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: IndexOpsConfig) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._config.workdir = os.path.realpath(config.workdir)
        self._timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

        # Kept across runs: sample files are resolved relative to their definition file
        self._dbs = DbCache()
        self._script = ScriptRecorder(self.work_dir)
        self._paths: Optional[BuildPaths] = None
        self._input: Optional[str] = None
        self._inputs: list[str] = []
        self._limits: dict = {}
        # Tasks of the last run(), keyed by part name (see plan_file)
        self._tasks: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self._task_dirs: set[str] = set()

        logger.debug(f"Init {type(self).__name__}")
        logger.debug("workdir: " + self.work_dir)

        for d in (self.work_dir, self.log_dir, self.asset_dir):
            os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)

    # ---
    # PROPERTIES

    @property
    def config(self) -> IndexOpsConfig:
        return self._config

    @property
    def work_dir(self) -> str:
        return self.config.workdir

    @property
    def asset_dir(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.work_dir, "assets")

    @property
    def log_dir(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.work_dir, "logs")

    @property
    def timestamp(self) -> str:
        return self._timestamp

    @property
    def paths(self) -> Optional[BuildPaths]:
        """Layout of the session of the last ``run()``."""
        return self._paths

    # ---
    # PUBLIC METHODS

    @property
    def tasks(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
        """Tasks planned by the last ``run()``, as written to ``plan.yaml``."""
        return self._tasks

    def write_plan(
        self,
        cluster: Optional[dict] = None,
        notify: Optional[str] = None,
        notify_level: str = "global",
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """Write the scripts of the last ``run()`` and ``plan.yaml``; return its path.

        Under ``assets/<session>/``, one directory per task (``<shard>/``):
        one script per kmtricks run, ``publish.sh`` (publication and cleanup),
        their sample lists and merge inputs. With ``cluster`` (a loaded
        ``--cluster`` file), also ``slurm/``: the files submitting the jobs,
        mailing ``notify`` at ``notify_level`` (``global`` or ``shard``).
        """
        if self._paths is None or self._input is None:
            logger.warning("Nothing planned: no plan written")
            return None
        if not self._tasks:
            # a finished session: its plan, scripts and states stay as they are
            logger.info(
                "Nothing to plan: every sample is already in its shard; "
                f"the previous plan is kept ({self._paths.plan})"
            )
            return None
        if cluster:
            # before anything is written: a plan without its submission files is useless
            check_type(cluster.get("type"), cluster.get("source", "cluster file"))
        self._script.write(self._paths.assets)
        groups = set(self._script.groups)
        per_job = self.config.chunks_per_job
        for task in self._tasks.values():
            has_publish = ScriptRecorder.publish_group(task["dir"]) in groups
            if not has_publish:
                task.pop("publish", None)
            task["jobs"] = job_names(task["shard"], list(task["chunks"]), has_publish, per_job)
        options = {
            "limits": self._limits,
            "chunks_per_job": per_job,
            "skip_compression": self.config.kmindex_skip_compression,
            "keep_previous": self.config.keep_previous,
            "base_path": self.config.sample_rootpath,
        }
        plan = new_plan(
            self._input,
            self.work_dir,
            self._paths.session,
            self._inputs + ([cluster["source"]] if cluster else []),
            options,
            {name: _task_entry(t) for name, t in self._tasks.items()},
        )
        if cluster:
            plan["cluster"] = dict(cluster, notify={"email": notify, "level": notify_level})
        write_plan(self._paths.plan, plan)
        if cluster:
            written = write_submission(
                plan, cluster, self._paths.assets, notify, notify_level
            )
            for path in written:
                logger.debug(f"Written {path}")
            submit = next((p for p in written if p.endswith("submit.sh")), None)
            if submit:
                logger.info(f"Submit the jobs with: bash {submit}")
        return self._paths.plan

    def run(
        self,
        path: str,
        mode: ApplyMode,
        fail_on_error: bool = False,
        report_path: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> ApplyResult:
        """Plan an index definition or span registry file against the kmindex registry.

        Plans every selected definition, then the publication of every target.

        Args:
            path: Path to a YAML or JSON file containing either an
                ``IndexDefinition`` or a span registry.
            mode: ``PLAN``, or ``DRY_RUN`` to skip the sample file checks.
            report_path: Where to write the YAML report, updated as the run
                goes (after each definition and each publish) and at the end.
            fail_on_error: Abort this run on the first build or publish error
                instead of continuing and returning ``PARTIAL``.

        Returns:
            An ``ApplyResult`` with the overall status and a per-index details
            dict. Status is ``SUCCESS`` when all operations complete without
            error, ``PARTIAL`` when some fail (only when
            ``fail_on_error=False``), or ``FAILED`` when a fatal error occurs.
        """
        if mode.executes:
            raise ValueError("IndexOps only plans: `apply` runs the plan")
        path = os.path.realpath(path)
        self._script = ScriptRecorder(self.work_dir)
        self._paths = paths = BuildPaths.for_input(self.work_dir, path)
        self._input = path
        self._tasks = {}
        self._task_dirs = set()
        report = RunReport(path, mode, self.config, report_path)
        report.set_build_dir(self.work_dir, paths.assets)
        self._limits = report.result.details["limits"]
        samples: Optional[SampleResolver] = None
        try:
            samples = self._run(report, path, mode, fail_on_error)
        finally:
            report.close()
            # not the layout: each new session rewrites it, which must not make
            # the plans of the previous sessions stale
            self._inputs = [path] + self._dbs.paths + (samples.files_read if samples else [])
        return report.result

    # ---
    # PRIVATE METHODS

    def _run(
        self, report: RunReport, path: str, mode: ApplyMode, fail_on_error: bool
    ) -> Optional[SampleResolver]:
        paths = self._paths
        assert paths is not None
        idt = IndexDefinitionTools()

        input_type, data = detect_input(path, idt)
        report.set_input_type(input_type)
        if data is None or input_type is ApplyInputType.UNKNOWN:
            logger.error("Could not retrieve data type.")
            report.result.status = ApplyStatus.FAILED
            return None

        os.makedirs(paths.assets, exist_ok=True)
        builder = IndexBuilder(
            workdir=self.work_dir,
            registry_name=paths.registry,
            data_folder=paths.runs,
            log_folder=self.log_dir,
            assets_folder=os.path.relpath(paths.assets, self.work_dir),
        )
        try:
            plan = SOURCES[input_type](self.config, self._dbs).load(path, idt, data)
            targets = self._targets(plan)
            for name in targets:
                check_index_name(name)
        except Exception as e:
            Log.handle_exception(logger, e, f"Failed to load definition file '{path}'")
            report.result.status = ApplyStatus.FAILED
            return None

        layout = LayoutStore.next_to(path)
        executor = IndexExecutor(builder, self.config, self._script, paths)
        samples = SampleResolver(
            self.config.sample_rootpath, mode.checks_files, self._dbs
        )

        own_targets = {t for t, parts in targets.items() if parts == [t]}
        built: dict[str, _Built] = {}
        for i in plan.definitions:
            assert i.name  # WorkPlan only holds named definitions
            logger.info(f"► Processing index definition '{i.name}'...")
            if i.name in own_targets and executor.has_index(i.name):
                logger.info(f"  └── {i.name} found in registry: skip")
                report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.NONE)
                continue
            try:
                target = plan.script_of(i.name)
                self._select_task(executor, target, target)
                b = self._build(report, executor, samples, i, layout, target)
                if b:
                    built[i.name] = b
            except Exception as e:
                msg = f"   Failed to plan index '{i.name}'"
                if report.fail(e, msg, i.name, fail_on_error):
                    return samples
            report.dump()

        for target, parts in targets.items():
            try:
                self._select_task(executor, plan.script_of(parts[0]), target)
                self._publish(report, executor, target, parts, built)
            except Exception as e:
                msg = f"Failed to plan the publication of '{target}'"
                if target in executor.publish_details:
                    report.record_publish(target, executor.publish_details[target])
                if report.fail(e, msg, target, fail_on_error):
                    return samples
            report.dump()

        report.finish()
        return samples

    def _select_task(self, executor: IndexExecutor, task_dir: str, target: str) -> None:
        """Record into ``assets/<session>/<task_dir>/`` (see ``_reset_task_dir``)."""
        executor.set_task(task_dir, target)

    def _reset_task_dir(self, task_dir: str) -> None:
        """Empty ``assets/<session>/<task_dir>/`` once, when something is planned
        in it: a shard found already built keeps the files of its build."""
        assert self._paths is not None
        if task_dir not in self._task_dirs:
            self._task_dirs.add(task_dir)
            shutil.rmtree(self._paths.task(task_dir), ignore_errors=True)

    @staticmethod
    def _targets(plan: WorkPlan) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Every index to publish, with the definitions it is made of.

        The merges of a span registry, plus every definition that is not a
        part of one of them (an index definition, or a part selected without
        its target), which is its own target.
        """
        targets = dict(plan.merges)
        in_merge = {p for parts in targets.values() for p in parts}
        for i in plan.definitions:
            if i.name and i.name not in in_merge:
                targets.setdefault(i.name, [i.name])
        return targets

    @staticmethod
    def _store_params(i: IndexDefinition, params: BuildParams) -> None:
        """Keep the size estimates of ``i`` in line with what is built."""
        i.partition_count = params.partitions

    def _resolve_params(
        self, i: IndexDefinition, sample_count: int, layout: LayoutStore, target: str
    ) -> BuildParams:
        params = resolve_build_params(i, sample_count, self.config, layout, target)
        # Keeps size estimates of i in line with what is built
        i.partition_count = params.partitions
        return params

    def _build(
        self,
        report: RunReport,
        executor: IndexExecutor,
        samples: SampleResolver,
        i: IndexDefinition,
        layout: LayoutStore,
        target: str,
    ) -> Optional[_Built]:
        """Build the runs of index ``i`` and record its outcome in ``report``."""
        # Partitions must be known before estimating the size
        params = self._resolve_params(i, i.sample_count, layout, target)
        size = i.get_stored_size()
        report.add_span_stats(i.span, i.sample_count, size.byte_count)
        logger.info(f"  └── Sample count: {i.sample_count}")
        logger.info(f"  └── Estimated build size: {size}")

        validate_definition(i)
        assert i.name is not None
        if not executor.claim(i.name):
            report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.NONE)
            return None

        fof, issues = samples.build_fof(i)
        sample_count = fof.get_sample_count()
        if sample_count == 0:
            logger.warning(
                f"{indent_prefix(logger)}Skipping index '{i.name}' as no sample was added to it"
            )
            status = ApplyStatus.FAILED if issues else ApplyStatus.NONE
            report.record(i.name, status, issues=issues)
            return None

        # A part already in its target (rerun of a finished or interrupted session)
        published = executor.index_samples(target)
        overlap = published.intersection(fof.samples)
        if overlap and len(overlap) == sample_count:
            logger.info(
                f"  └── All samples of '{i.name}' are already in '{target}': skip"
            )
            report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.NONE, issues=issues)
            return None
        if overlap:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{len(overlap)} of the {sample_count} samples of '{i.name}' are "
                f"already in '{target}' ({summarize_names(sorted(overlap))}): "
                f"a sample can only be added once"
            )

        # Samples may have been skipped since the estimate: resolve for the actual count
        if sample_count != i.sample_count:
            # i.partition_count now holds the first count: keep its source
            source = params.partitions_source
            params = self._resolve_params(i, sample_count, layout, target)
            params = replace(params, partitions_source=source)
        params = executor.align_with(target, params, i.name)
        self._store_params(i, params)
        report.record_params(i.name, i, params, sample_count)
        assert self._paths is not None
        report.record_script(i.name, self._paths.task(target))
        self._reset_task_dir(target)
        try:
            runs = executor.build(i, fof, params)
        finally:
            report.record_runs(
                i.name,
                {
                    r: executor.run_details[r]
                    for r in executor.run_names
                    if r in executor.run_details
                    and (r == i.name or r.startswith(f"{i.name}_chunk"))
                },
            )
        report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.SUCCESS, issues=issues)
        self._tasks[i.name] = {
            "shard": target,
            "dir": target,
            "samples": sample_count,
            "span": i.span,
            "partitions": params.partitions,
            "minim_size": params.minim_size,
            "threads": params.threads,
            "chunks": {r: {"samples": n} for r, n in runs.items()},
        }
        return _Built(i, params, runs)

    def _publish(
        self,
        report: RunReport,
        executor: IndexExecutor,
        target: str,
        parts: list[str],
        built: dict[str, _Built],
    ) -> None:
        """Plan the publication of the runs of ``parts`` as ``target``.

        A folder ``BUILD_DIR/<target>`` left unregistered by an interrupted
        publish, with nothing new to add, is registered.
        """
        new = [built[p] for p in parts if p in built]
        failed = [
            p
            for p in parts
            if p not in built and report.result_of(p) == ApplyStatus.FAILED.value
        ]
        if failed:
            logger.warning(
                f"Cannot publish '{target}': {summarize_names(failed)} failed to plan"
            )
            if parts != [target]:
                report.fold_publish(target, parts)
            return

        registered = executor.has_index(target)
        # What the publish script assumes of the registry; checked by apply
        expects = {
            "registered": registered,
            "samples": len(executor.index_samples(target)) if registered else 0,
        }
        if not new:
            if executor.has_folder(target) and not registered:
                logger.info(f"► Registering '{target}' (publish interrupted)...")
                self._reset_task_dir(executor.task_dir)
                executor.register_folder(target, parts)
            self._record_publish(report, executor, target, parts, expects)
            return

        if len(new) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'{target}' gets {len(new)} parts in one session "
                f"({summarize_names([b.definition.name for b in new])}): one is expected"
            )
        logger.info(f"► Publishing '{target}'...")
        self._reset_task_dir(executor.task_dir)
        executor.publish(new[0].definition, target, new[0].runs, new[0].params)
        self._record_publish(report, executor, target, parts, expects)

    def _record_publish(
        self,
        report: RunReport,
        executor: IndexExecutor,
        target: str,
        parts: list[str],
        expects: dict,
    ) -> None:
        assert self._paths is not None
        details = dict(executor.publish_details.get(target, {}))
        if details:
            task_dir = executor.task_dir
            details["publish_script"] = os.path.join(
                self._paths.task(task_dir), f"{PUBLISH}.sh"
            )
            report.record_publish(target, details)
            part = next((p for p in parts if p in self._tasks), parts[0])
            task = self._tasks.setdefault(
                part,
                {"shard": target, "dir": task_dir, "samples": 0, "chunks": {}},
            )
            publish = details.get("publish", {})
            task["publish"] = {"script": f"{PUBLISH}.sh", "expects": expects, **publish}
        if parts != [target]:
            report.fold_publish(target, parts)

    def write_plan(
    self,
    cluster: Optional[dict] = None,
    notify: Optional[str] = None,
    notify_level: str = "global",
) -> Optional[str]:
    """Write the scripts of the last ``run()`` and ``plan.yaml``; return its path.

    Under ``assets/<session>/``, one directory per task (``<shard>/``):
    one script per kmtricks run, ``publish.sh`` (publication and cleanup),
    their sample lists and merge inputs. With ``cluster`` (a loaded
    ``--cluster`` file), also ``slurm/``: the files submitting the jobs,
    mailing ``notify`` at ``notify_level`` (``global`` or ``shard``).
    """
    if self._paths is None or self._input is None:
        logger.warning("Nothing planned: no plan written")
        return None
    if not self._tasks:
        # a finished session: its plan, scripts and states stay as they are
        logger.info(
            "Nothing to plan: every sample is already in its shard; "
            f"the previous plan is kept ({self._paths.plan})"
        )
        return None
    if cluster:
        # before anything is written: a plan without its submission files is useless
        check_type(cluster.get("type"), cluster.get("source", "cluster file"))
    self._script.write(self._paths.assets)
    groups = set(self._script.groups)
    per_job = self.config.chunks_per_job
    for task in self._tasks.values():
        has_publish = ScriptRecorder.publish_group(task["dir"]) in groups
        if not has_publish:
            task.pop("publish", None)
        task["jobs"] = job_names(task["shard"], list(task["chunks"]), has_publish, per_job)
    options = {
        "limits": self._limits,
        "chunks_per_job": per_job,
        "skip_compression": self.config.kmindex_skip_compression,
        "keep_previous": self.config.keep_previous,
        "base_path": self.config.sample_rootpath,
    }
    plan = new_plan(
        self._input,
        self.work_dir,
        self._paths.session,
        self._inputs + ([cluster["source"]] if cluster else []),
        options,
        {name: _task_entry(t) for name, t in self._tasks.items()},
    )
    if cluster:
        plan["cluster"] = dict(cluster, notify={"email": notify, "level": notify_level})
    write_plan(self._paths.plan, plan)
    if cluster:
        written = write_submission(
            plan, cluster, self._paths.assets, notify, notify_level
        )
        for path in written:
            logger.debug(f"Written {path}")
        submit = next((p for p in written if p.endswith("submit.sh")), None)
        if submit:
            logger.info(f"Submit the jobs with: bash {submit}")
    return self._paths.plan

    def run(
    self,
    path: str,
    mode: ApplyMode,
    fail_on_error: bool = False,
    report_path: Optional[str] = None,
) -> ApplyResult:
    """Plan an index definition or span registry file against the kmindex registry.

    Plans every selected definition, then the publication of every target.

    Args:
        path: Path to a YAML or JSON file containing either an
            ``IndexDefinition`` or a span registry.
        mode: ``PLAN``, or ``DRY_RUN`` to skip the sample file checks.
        report_path: Where to write the YAML report, updated as the run
            goes (after each definition and each publish) and at the end.
        fail_on_error: Abort this run on the first build or publish error
            instead of continuing and returning ``PARTIAL``.

    Returns:
        An ``ApplyResult`` with the overall status and a per-index details
        dict. Status is ``SUCCESS`` when all operations complete without
        error, ``PARTIAL`` when some fail (only when
        ``fail_on_error=False``), or ``FAILED`` when a fatal error occurs.
    """
    if mode.executes:
        raise ValueError("IndexOps only plans: `apply` runs the plan")
    path = os.path.realpath(path)
    self._script = ScriptRecorder(self.work_dir)
    self._paths = paths = BuildPaths.for_input(self.work_dir, path)
    self._input = path
    self._tasks = {}
    self._task_dirs = set()
    report = RunReport(path, mode, self.config, report_path)
    report.set_build_dir(self.work_dir, paths.assets)
    self._limits = report.result.details["limits"]
    samples: Optional[SampleResolver] = None
    try:
        samples = self._run(report, path, mode, fail_on_error)
    finally:
        report.close()
        # not the layout: each new session rewrites it, which must not make
        # the plans of the previous sessions stale
        self._inputs = [path] + self._dbs.paths + (samples.files_read if samples else [])
    return report.result

    BuildParams dataclass

    Resolved kmindex build parameters for one index.

    partitions and minim_size are invariants of a shard: indexes are only mergeable when they share them. The minimizer size is fixed at design; the partition count by the design (-p) or by the first build of the shard (see resolve_partitions). chunk_size is set when the open-files ceiling can't fit every sample in one kmtricks build; the build is then split into chunks of at most that many samples, which are merged.

    partitions_source tells where the partition count comes from, for the report: published (the layout records the count of the shard), design (compose -P), auto (sized from the limits), registered (the shard already built) or run (a run of the session already started). It does not take part in comparisons.

    def clamp_partitions(count: int) -> int:
    """Apply the kmtricks partition floor; 0 (auto) is left untouched."""
    return max(count, KMTRICKS_MIN_PARTITIONS) if count > 0 else count

    types (IndexOpsConfig, ApplyResult, …) is shared by most modules and left out of the diagram.

    A build on a cluster

    With plan --cluster FILE, cluster.write_slurm writes BUILD_DIR/assets/<session>/slurm/ next to the plan. submit.sh submits what apply --pending lists; every job runs apply --task <job>.

    sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant plan as kmhelpers plan
    participant submit as submit.sh
    participant build as build.sbatch<br/>(array)
    participant publish as publish.sbatch<br/>(one per shard)
    participant finish as finish.sbatch

    User->>plan: --cluster cluster.yaml
    plan-->>User: plan.yaml, task scripts, slurm/
    User->>submit: bash slurm/submit.sh
    submit->>submit: apply --pending
    submit->>build: sbatch --array (jobs.build)
    submit->>publish: sbatch, afterok on the shard's array tasks (jobs.publish)
    submit->>finish: sbatch, afterany on every job (jobs.check)
    build->>build: apply --task SHARD_jK
    publish->>publish: apply --task SHARD_publish
    finish->>finish: manage check, apply --status, mail

    A shard whose chunks fit in one job (see plan_file.job_names) has no separate publish job: its single job runs its chunks then its publish step in the build array, with the build resources.

    Cluster file and job kinds

    The cluster file (plan --cluster) sets the resources of each job kind. cluster.load_cluster resolves each kind from:

    1. the top-level keys (partition, time, exclude, account, qos, constraint, cpus, mem, extra), defaults for every kind;
    2. jobs.<kind>, which overrides them;
    3. for check only, CHECK_DEFAULTS (1 CPU, 4G) under jobs.check.

    build and publish must end up with cpus and mem. An unknown kind under jobs is an error.

    Kind Script Sizes the plan
    build build.sbatch (array, one task per build job) yes: limits_for(cluster, "build") in cli/plan.py
    publish publish.sbatch (one per split shard) yes: limits_for(cluster, "publish")
    check finish.sbatch no

    For example, to send the publish and finish jobs to other partitions:

    partition: long                 # every kind
jobs:
  build:   {cpus: 24, mem: 120G}
  publish: {cpus: 24, mem: 120G, partition: bigmem}
  check:   {cpus: 1, mem: 4G, time: "1:00:00", partition: short}

    The #SBATCH lines are written by plan, so run plan again after editing the cluster file. For a one-off change, an option on the command line wins over the script's: sbatch -p bigmem slurm/publish.sbatch <shard>_publish.

    Adding a job kind

    A kind is only a resource profile; it does nothing until a script uses it. In cluster.py:

    1. Add it to JOB_KINDS. If it should not require cpus and mem, give it defaults as check has (CHECK_DEFAULTS, applied in load_cluster).
    2. Write its script in write_slurm: an entry of files built from _sbatch_lines(cluster["jobs"]["<kind>"], ...), body_head and its command.
    3. Submit it in _submit_script: sbatch with its dependencies, a line in submitted.tsv, and its id in ALL so that finish waits for it. If it must not be submitted twice, check active as finish does.
    4. If its jobs size themselves from --limits, pass limits_for(cluster, "<kind>", safety_margin) to the plan in cli/plan.py.
    5. If it runs a new step of the plan (as publish runs PUBLISH), the plan must name it too: plan_file.job_names and the steps runner.PlanRunner runs. A kind that wraps an existing command (e.g. kmhelpers manage ...) only changes cluster.py.
    6. Update the docstring of cluster.py, this page, and tests/test_cluster.py.

    class IndexOps:
    """Plans k-mer index builds against the kmindex registry ``BUILD_DIR``.

    Loads an index definition or a span registry (see ``sources``), plans
    every selected definition as unregistered kmtricks runs, then the
    publication of each target: the runs of its parts, merged with its
    current version when it is already registered, become
    ``BUILD_DIR/<target>``. A definition that is not a part of a selected
    merge is its own target. Nothing is built: ``write_plan()`` writes the
    scripts of every task and ``plan.yaml``, which ``apply`` runs
    (``runner.PlanRunner``).

    Args:
        config: Runtime configuration governing paths, build parameters,
            filtering, and execution behaviour.  See ``IndexOpsConfig``.

    Attributes:
        config (IndexOpsConfig): The resolved configuration (``workdir`` is
            made absolute on construction).
        work_dir (str): ``BUILD_DIR``, the kmindex registry.
        asset_dir (str): ``<work_dir>/assets`` - one folder of scripts per session.
        log_dir (str): ``<work_dir>/logs`` - log file destination.
        timestamp (str): ``YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS`` string captured at construction.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: IndexOpsConfig) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._config.workdir = os.path.realpath(config.workdir)
        self._timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

        # Kept across runs: sample files are resolved relative to their definition file
        self._dbs = DbCache()
        self._script = ScriptRecorder(self.work_dir)
        self._paths: Optional[BuildPaths] = None
        self._input: Optional[str] = None
        self._inputs: list[str] = []
        self._limits: dict = {}
        # Tasks of the last run(), keyed by part name (see plan_file)
        self._tasks: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self._task_dirs: set[str] = set()

        logger.debug(f"Init {type(self).__name__}")
        logger.debug("workdir: " + self.work_dir)

        for d in (self.work_dir, self.log_dir, self.asset_dir):
            os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)

    # ---
    # PROPERTIES

    @property
    def config(self) -> IndexOpsConfig:
        return self._config

    @property
    def work_dir(self) -> str:
        return self.config.workdir

    @property
    def asset_dir(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.work_dir, "assets")

    @property
    def log_dir(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.work_dir, "logs")

    @property
    def timestamp(self) -> str:
        return self._timestamp

    @property
    def paths(self) -> Optional[BuildPaths]:
        """Layout of the session of the last ``run()``."""
        return self._paths

    # ---
    # PUBLIC METHODS

    @property
    def tasks(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
        """Tasks planned by the last ``run()``, as written to ``plan.yaml``."""
        return self._tasks

    def write_plan(
        self,
        cluster: Optional[dict] = None,
        notify: Optional[str] = None,
        notify_level: str = "global",
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """Write the scripts of the last ``run()`` and ``plan.yaml``; return its path.

        Under ``assets/<session>/``, one directory per task (``<shard>/``):
        one script per kmtricks run, ``publish.sh`` (publication and cleanup),
        their sample lists and merge inputs. With ``cluster`` (a loaded
        ``--cluster`` file), also ``slurm/``: the files submitting the jobs,
        mailing ``notify`` at ``notify_level`` (``global`` or ``shard``).
        """
        if self._paths is None or self._input is None:
            logger.warning("Nothing planned: no plan written")
            return None
        if not self._tasks:
            # a finished session: its plan, scripts and states stay as they are
            logger.info(
                "Nothing to plan: every sample is already in its shard; "
                f"the previous plan is kept ({self._paths.plan})"
            )
            return None
        if cluster:
            # before anything is written: a plan without its submission files is useless
            check_type(cluster.get("type"), cluster.get("source", "cluster file"))
        self._script.write(self._paths.assets)
        groups = set(self._script.groups)
        per_job = self.config.chunks_per_job
        for task in self._tasks.values():
            has_publish = ScriptRecorder.publish_group(task["dir"]) in groups
            if not has_publish:
                task.pop("publish", None)
            task["jobs"] = job_names(task["shard"], list(task["chunks"]), has_publish, per_job)
        options = {
            "limits": self._limits,
            "chunks_per_job": per_job,
            "skip_compression": self.config.kmindex_skip_compression,
            "keep_previous": self.config.keep_previous,
            "base_path": self.config.sample_rootpath,
        }
        plan = new_plan(
            self._input,
            self.work_dir,
            self._paths.session,
            self._inputs + ([cluster["source"]] if cluster else []),
            options,
            {name: _task_entry(t) for name, t in self._tasks.items()},
        )
        if cluster:
            plan["cluster"] = dict(cluster, notify={"email": notify, "level": notify_level})
        write_plan(self._paths.plan, plan)
        if cluster:
            written = write_submission(
                plan, cluster, self._paths.assets, notify, notify_level
            )
            for path in written:
                logger.debug(f"Written {path}")
            submit = next((p for p in written if p.endswith("submit.sh")), None)
            if submit:
                logger.info(f"Submit the jobs with: bash {submit}")
        return self._paths.plan

    def run(
        self,
        path: str,
        mode: ApplyMode,
        fail_on_error: bool = False,
        report_path: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> ApplyResult:
        """Plan an index definition or span registry file against the kmindex registry.

        Plans every selected definition, then the publication of every target.

        Args:
            path: Path to a YAML or JSON file containing either an
                ``IndexDefinition`` or a span registry.
            mode: ``PLAN``, or ``DRY_RUN`` to skip the sample file checks.
            report_path: Where to write the YAML report, updated as the run
                goes (after each definition and each publish) and at the end.
            fail_on_error: Abort this run on the first build or publish error
                instead of continuing and returning ``PARTIAL``.

        Returns:
            An ``ApplyResult`` with the overall status and a per-index details
            dict. Status is ``SUCCESS`` when all operations complete without
            error, ``PARTIAL`` when some fail (only when
            ``fail_on_error=False``), or ``FAILED`` when a fatal error occurs.
        """
        if mode.executes:
            raise ValueError("IndexOps only plans: `apply` runs the plan")
        path = os.path.realpath(path)
        self._script = ScriptRecorder(self.work_dir)
        self._paths = paths = BuildPaths.for_input(self.work_dir, path)
        self._input = path
        self._tasks = {}
        self._task_dirs = set()
        report = RunReport(path, mode, self.config, report_path)
        report.set_build_dir(self.work_dir, paths.assets)
        self._limits = report.result.details["limits"]
        samples: Optional[SampleResolver] = None
        try:
            samples = self._run(report, path, mode, fail_on_error)
        finally:
            report.close()
            # not the layout: each new session rewrites it, which must not make
            # the plans of the previous sessions stale
            self._inputs = [path] + self._dbs.paths + (samples.files_read if samples else [])
        return report.result

    # ---
    # PRIVATE METHODS

    def _run(
        self, report: RunReport, path: str, mode: ApplyMode, fail_on_error: bool
    ) -> Optional[SampleResolver]:
        paths = self._paths
        assert paths is not None
        idt = IndexDefinitionTools()

        input_type, data = detect_input(path, idt)
        report.set_input_type(input_type)
        if data is None or input_type is ApplyInputType.UNKNOWN:
            logger.error("Could not retrieve data type.")
            report.result.status = ApplyStatus.FAILED
            return None

        os.makedirs(paths.assets, exist_ok=True)
        builder = IndexBuilder(
            workdir=self.work_dir,
            registry_name=paths.registry,
            data_folder=paths.runs,
            log_folder=self.log_dir,
            assets_folder=os.path.relpath(paths.assets, self.work_dir),
        )
        try:
            plan = SOURCES[input_type](self.config, self._dbs).load(path, idt, data)
            targets = self._targets(plan)
            for name in targets:
                check_index_name(name)
        except Exception as e:
            Log.handle_exception(logger, e, f"Failed to load definition file '{path}'")
            report.result.status = ApplyStatus.FAILED
            return None

        layout = LayoutStore.next_to(path)
        executor = IndexExecutor(builder, self.config, self._script, paths)
        samples = SampleResolver(
            self.config.sample_rootpath, mode.checks_files, self._dbs
        )

        own_targets = {t for t, parts in targets.items() if parts == [t]}
        built: dict[str, _Built] = {}
        for i in plan.definitions:
            assert i.name  # WorkPlan only holds named definitions
            logger.info(f"► Processing index definition '{i.name}'...")
            if i.name in own_targets and executor.has_index(i.name):
                logger.info(f"  └── {i.name} found in registry: skip")
                report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.NONE)
                continue
            try:
                target = plan.script_of(i.name)
                self._select_task(executor, target, target)
                b = self._build(report, executor, samples, i, layout, target)
                if b:
                    built[i.name] = b
            except Exception as e:
                msg = f"   Failed to plan index '{i.name}'"
                if report.fail(e, msg, i.name, fail_on_error):
                    return samples
            report.dump()

        for target, parts in targets.items():
            try:
                self._select_task(executor, plan.script_of(parts[0]), target)
                self._publish(report, executor, target, parts, built)
            except Exception as e:
                msg = f"Failed to plan the publication of '{target}'"
                if target in executor.publish_details:
                    report.record_publish(target, executor.publish_details[target])
                if report.fail(e, msg, target, fail_on_error):
                    return samples
            report.dump()

        report.finish()
        return samples

    def _select_task(self, executor: IndexExecutor, task_dir: str, target: str) -> None:
        """Record into ``assets/<session>/<task_dir>/`` (see ``_reset_task_dir``)."""
        executor.set_task(task_dir, target)

    def _reset_task_dir(self, task_dir: str) -> None:
        """Empty ``assets/<session>/<task_dir>/`` once, when something is planned
        in it: a shard found already built keeps the files of its build."""
        assert self._paths is not None
        if task_dir not in self._task_dirs:
            self._task_dirs.add(task_dir)
            shutil.rmtree(self._paths.task(task_dir), ignore_errors=True)

    @staticmethod
    def _targets(plan: WorkPlan) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Every index to publish, with the definitions it is made of.

        The merges of a span registry, plus every definition that is not a
        part of one of them (an index definition, or a part selected without
        its target), which is its own target.
        """
        targets = dict(plan.merges)
        in_merge = {p for parts in targets.values() for p in parts}
        for i in plan.definitions:
            if i.name and i.name not in in_merge:
                targets.setdefault(i.name, [i.name])
        return targets

    @staticmethod
    def _store_params(i: IndexDefinition, params: BuildParams) -> None:
        """Keep the size estimates of ``i`` in line with what is built."""
        i.partition_count = params.partitions

    def _resolve_params(
        self, i: IndexDefinition, sample_count: int, layout: LayoutStore, target: str
    ) -> BuildParams:
        params = resolve_build_params(i, sample_count, self.config, layout, target)
        # Keeps size estimates of i in line with what is built
        i.partition_count = params.partitions
        return params

    def _build(
        self,
        report: RunReport,
        executor: IndexExecutor,
        samples: SampleResolver,
        i: IndexDefinition,
        layout: LayoutStore,
        target: str,
    ) -> Optional[_Built]:
        """Build the runs of index ``i`` and record its outcome in ``report``."""
        # Partitions must be known before estimating the size
        params = self._resolve_params(i, i.sample_count, layout, target)
        size = i.get_stored_size()
        report.add_span_stats(i.span, i.sample_count, size.byte_count)
        logger.info(f"  └── Sample count: {i.sample_count}")
        logger.info(f"  └── Estimated build size: {size}")

        validate_definition(i)
        assert i.name is not None
        if not executor.claim(i.name):
            report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.NONE)
            return None

        fof, issues = samples.build_fof(i)
        sample_count = fof.get_sample_count()
        if sample_count == 0:
            logger.warning(
                f"{indent_prefix(logger)}Skipping index '{i.name}' as no sample was added to it"
            )
            status = ApplyStatus.FAILED if issues else ApplyStatus.NONE
            report.record(i.name, status, issues=issues)
            return None

        # A part already in its target (rerun of a finished or interrupted session)
        published = executor.index_samples(target)
        overlap = published.intersection(fof.samples)
        if overlap and len(overlap) == sample_count:
            logger.info(
                f"  └── All samples of '{i.name}' are already in '{target}': skip"
            )
            report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.NONE, issues=issues)
            return None
        if overlap:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{len(overlap)} of the {sample_count} samples of '{i.name}' are "
                f"already in '{target}' ({summarize_names(sorted(overlap))}): "
                f"a sample can only be added once"
            )

        # Samples may have been skipped since the estimate: resolve for the actual count
        if sample_count != i.sample_count:
            # i.partition_count now holds the first count: keep its source
            source = params.partitions_source
            params = self._resolve_params(i, sample_count, layout, target)
            params = replace(params, partitions_source=source)
        params = executor.align_with(target, params, i.name)
        self._store_params(i, params)
        report.record_params(i.name, i, params, sample_count)
        assert self._paths is not None
        report.record_script(i.name, self._paths.task(target))
        self._reset_task_dir(target)
        try:
            runs = executor.build(i, fof, params)
        finally:
            report.record_runs(
                i.name,
                {
                    r: executor.run_details[r]
                    for r in executor.run_names
                    if r in executor.run_details
                    and (r == i.name or r.startswith(f"{i.name}_chunk"))
                },
            )
        report.record(i.name, ApplyStatus.SUCCESS, issues=issues)
        self._tasks[i.name] = {
            "shard": target,
            "dir": target,
            "samples": sample_count,
            "span": i.span,
            "partitions": params.partitions,
            "minim_size": params.minim_size,
            "threads": params.threads,
            "chunks": {r: {"samples": n} for r, n in runs.items()},
        }
        return _Built(i, params, runs)

    def _publish(
        self,
        report: RunReport,
        executor: IndexExecutor,
        target: str,
        parts: list[str],
        built: dict[str, _Built],
    ) -> None:
        """Plan the publication of the runs of ``parts`` as ``target``.

        A folder ``BUILD_DIR/<target>`` left unregistered by an interrupted
        publish, with nothing new to add, is registered.
        """
        new = [built[p] for p in parts if p in built]
        failed = [
            p
            for p in parts
            if p not in built and report.result_of(p) == ApplyStatus.FAILED.value
        ]
        if failed:
            logger.warning(
                f"Cannot publish '{target}': {summarize_names(failed)} failed to plan"
            )
            if parts != [target]:
                report.fold_publish(target, parts)
            return

        registered = executor.has_index(target)
        # What the publish script assumes of the registry; checked by apply
        expects = {
            "registered": registered,
            "samples": len(executor.index_samples(target)) if registered else 0,
        }
        if not new:
            if executor.has_folder(target) and not registered:
                logger.info(f"► Registering '{target}' (publish interrupted)...")
                self._reset_task_dir(executor.task_dir)
                executor.register_folder(target, parts)
            self._record_publish(report, executor, target, parts, expects)
            return

        if len(new) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'{target}' gets {len(new)} parts in one session "
                f"({summarize_names([b.definition.name for b in new])}): one is expected"
            )
        logger.info(f"► Publishing '{target}'...")
        self._reset_task_dir(executor.task_dir)
        executor.publish(new[0].definition, target, new[0].runs, new[0].params)
        self._record_publish(report, executor, target, parts, expects)

    def _record_publish(
        self,
        report: RunReport,
        executor: IndexExecutor,
        target: str,
        parts: list[str],
        expects: dict,
    ) -> None:
        assert self._paths is not None
        details = dict(executor.publish_details.get(target, {}))
        if details:
            task_dir = executor.task_dir
            details["publish_script"] = os.path.join(
                self._paths.task(task_dir), f"{PUBLISH}.sh"
            )
            report.record_publish(target, details)
            part = next((p for p in parts if p in self._tasks), parts[0])
            task = self._tasks.setdefault(
                part,
                {"shard": target, "dir": task_dir, "samples": 0, "chunks": {}},
            )
            publish = details.get("publish", {})
            task["publish"] = {"script": f"{PUBLISH}.sh", "expects": expects, **publish}
        if parts != [target]:
            report.fold_publish(target, parts)

    paths property

    Layout of the session of the last run().

    tasks property

    Tasks planned by the last run(), as written to plan.yaml.

    write_plan(cluster=None, notify=None, notify_level='global')

    Write the scripts of the last run() and plan.yaml; return its path.

    Under assets/<session>/, one directory per task (<shard>/): one script per kmtricks run, publish.sh (publication and cleanup), their sample lists and merge inputs. With cluster (a loaded --cluster file), also slurm/: the files submitting the jobs, mailing notify at notify_level (global or shard).

    def write_plan(
    self,
    cluster: Optional[dict] = None,
    notify: Optional[str] = None,
    notify_level: str = "global",
) -> Optional[str]:
    """Write the scripts of the last ``run()`` and ``plan.yaml``; return its path.

    Under ``assets/<session>/``, one directory per task (``<shard>/``):
    one script per kmtricks run, ``publish.sh`` (publication and cleanup),
    their sample lists and merge inputs. With ``cluster`` (a loaded
    ``--cluster`` file), also ``slurm/``: the files submitting the jobs,
    mailing ``notify`` at ``notify_level`` (``global`` or ``shard``).
    """
    if self._paths is None or self._input is None:
        logger.warning("Nothing planned: no plan written")
        return None
    if not self._tasks:
        # a finished session: its plan, scripts and states stay as they are
        logger.info(
            "Nothing to plan: every sample is already in its shard; "
            f"the previous plan is kept ({self._paths.plan})"
        )
        return None
    if cluster:
        # before anything is written: a plan without its submission files is useless
        check_type(cluster.get("type"), cluster.get("source", "cluster file"))
    self._script.write(self._paths.assets)
    groups = set(self._script.groups)
    per_job = self.config.chunks_per_job
    for task in self._tasks.values():
        has_publish = ScriptRecorder.publish_group(task["dir"]) in groups
        if not has_publish:
            task.pop("publish", None)
        task["jobs"] = job_names(task["shard"], list(task["chunks"]), has_publish, per_job)
    options = {
        "limits": self._limits,
        "chunks_per_job": per_job,
        "skip_compression": self.config.kmindex_skip_compression,
        "keep_previous": self.config.keep_previous,
        "base_path": self.config.sample_rootpath,
    }
    plan = new_plan(
        self._input,
        self.work_dir,
        self._paths.session,
        self._inputs + ([cluster["source"]] if cluster else []),
        options,
        {name: _task_entry(t) for name, t in self._tasks.items()},
    )
    if cluster:
        plan["cluster"] = dict(cluster, notify={"email": notify, "level": notify_level})
    write_plan(self._paths.plan, plan)
    if cluster:
        written = write_submission(
            plan, cluster, self._paths.assets, notify, notify_level
        )
        for path in written:
            logger.debug(f"Written {path}")
        submit = next((p for p in written if p.endswith("submit.sh")), None)
        if submit:
            logger.info(f"Submit the jobs with: bash {submit}")
    return self._paths.plan

    def run(
    self,
    path: str,
    mode: ApplyMode,
    fail_on_error: bool = False,
    report_path: Optional[str] = None,
) -> ApplyResult:
    """Plan an index definition or span registry file against the kmindex registry.

    Plans every selected definition, then the publication of every target.

    Args:
        path: Path to a YAML or JSON file containing either an
            ``IndexDefinition`` or a span registry.
        mode: ``PLAN``, or ``DRY_RUN`` to skip the sample file checks.
        report_path: Where to write the YAML report, updated as the run
            goes (after each definition and each publish) and at the end.
        fail_on_error: Abort this run on the first build or publish error
            instead of continuing and returning ``PARTIAL``.

    Returns:
        An ``ApplyResult`` with the overall status and a per-index details
        dict. Status is ``SUCCESS`` when all operations complete without
        error, ``PARTIAL`` when some fail (only when
        ``fail_on_error=False``), or ``FAILED`` when a fatal error occurs.
    """
    if mode.executes:
        raise ValueError("IndexOps only plans: `apply` runs the plan")
    path = os.path.realpath(path)
    self._script = ScriptRecorder(self.work_dir)
    self._paths = paths = BuildPaths.for_input(self.work_dir, path)
    self._input = path
    self._tasks = {}
    self._task_dirs = set()
    report = RunReport(path, mode, self.config, report_path)
    report.set_build_dir(self.work_dir, paths.assets)
    self._limits = report.result.details["limits"]
    samples: Optional[SampleResolver] = None
    try:
        samples = self._run(report, path, mode, fail_on_error)
    finally:
        report.close()
        # not the layout: each new session rewrites it, which must not make
        # the plans of the previous sessions stale
        self._inputs = [path] + self._dbs.paths + (samples.files_read if samples else [])
    return report.result

    pykmhelpers.pipeline.index_ops.plan_file

    The plan manifest, BUILD_DIR/assets/<session>/plan.yaml.

    plan writes it next to the scripts of every task; apply loads it and runs the scripts it lists. A task is one session's samples added to one index (<shard>_<session>, or an index definition), keyed by its part name::

    tasks:
  <part>:
    shard: <index in BUILD_DIR>
    dir: <shard>/                 scripts and fofs, under assets/<session>/
    samples, partitions, minim_size, threads, ...
    chunks: {<run>: {samples: n}} kmtricks runs, <dir>/<run>.sh
    publish: {script: publish.sh, expects, mode, steps, ...}
    jobs: {<job>: [<run>..., publish]}

    A job is what apply --task <job> and a SLURM array task run: some chunks of one task, or its publish step (PUBLISH).

    job_names(shard, chunks, has_publish, per_job)

    Jobs of one task: {job: [runs..., PUBLISH]}.

    per_job 0 (or at least the chunk count): one job <shard>, its chunks then its publish step. Else <shard>_j<k> jobs of up to per_job chunks, then <shard>_publish, run after all of them.

    def job_names(shard: str, chunks: list[str], has_publish: bool, per_job: int) -> dict:
    """Jobs of one task: ``{job: [runs..., PUBLISH]}``.

    ``per_job`` 0 (or at least the chunk count): one job ``<shard>``, its
    chunks then its publish step. Else ``<shard>_j<k>`` jobs of up to ``per_job``
    chunks, then ``<shard>_publish``, run after all of them.
    """
    if per_job <= 0 or len(chunks) <= per_job:
        return {shard: list(chunks) + ([PUBLISH] if has_publish else [])}
    jobs: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for k in range(math.ceil(len(chunks) / per_job)):
        jobs[f"{shard}_j{k}"] = list(chunks[k * per_job : (k + 1) * per_job])
    if has_publish:
        jobs[f"{shard}_publish"] = [PUBLISH]
    return jobs

    def file_hashes(paths: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """``{path: sha256}`` of the input files a plan was made from."""
    hashes = {}
    for path in sorted(set(os.path.realpath(p) for p in paths if p)):
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            hashes[path] = _sha256(path)
    return hashes

    def stale_files(hashes: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    """Input files of a plan that changed (or vanished) since it was made."""
    return [
        path
        for path, digest in hashes.items()
        if not os.path.isfile(path) or _sha256(path) != digest
    ]

    def load_plan(path: str) -> dict:
    """Load ``plan.yaml``; refuse a missing or foreign file."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"No plan at {path}: run `kmhelpers plan` with the same INPUT and -o first"
        )
    with open(path) as f:
        plan = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
    if plan.get("type") != PLAN_TYPE:
        raise ValueError(f"Not a kmhelpers plan: {path}")
    return plan

    def check_fresh(plan: dict, definition: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    """Refuse a plan made from other inputs, or by another kmhelpers version."""
    problems = []
    if definition and os.path.realpath(definition) != plan.get("definition"):
        problems.append(f"it was made for {plan.get('definition')}, not {definition}")
    if plan.get("kmhelpers") != pykmhelpers.__version__:
        problems.append(
            f"it was made by kmhelpers {plan.get('kmhelpers')}, "
            f"this is {pykmhelpers.__version__}"
        )
    changed = stale_files(plan.get("fingerprint", {}).get("files", {}))
    if changed:
        shown = ", ".join(changed[:3]) + (f" (+{len(changed) - 3})" if len(changed) > 3 else "")
        problems.append(f"its inputs changed: {shown}")
    if problems:
        raise ValueError(
            "The plan is stale: " + "; ".join(problems) + ". Run `kmhelpers plan` again."
        )

    The --cluster file of plan, and the SLURM files written from it.

    The file describes the scheduler and the resources of each kind of job::

    type: slurm
partition: compute
time: 2-00:00:00
exclude: [node01]
max_parallel: 8                   # build array tasks running at once
output: logs/slurm/%x_%A_%a.out   # relative to BUILD_DIR
setup: |                          # run before kmhelpers in every job
  export PATH=...
extra: []                         # other sbatch options, as is
jobs:
  build: {cpus: 24, mem: 120G}
  publish: {cpus: 24, mem: 120G}
  check: {cpus: 1, mem: 4G, time: "1:00:00"}
limits: {files: 131072, maps: 65530}   # compute-node limits, optional

    The plan is sized from it: chunks from jobs.build (threads = cpus, ram = mem), merges from jobs.publish, plus limits (else detected on the node plan runs on). write_slurm writes assets/<session>/slurm/.

    def mem_bytes(value) -> int:
    """``120G``, ``4096M`` or a number of MB (as sbatch) -> bytes."""
    m = _MEM.match(str(value).strip())
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid memory '{value}' (expected e.g. 120G, 4096M)")
    return int(float(m.group(1)) * _UNITS[m.group(2).upper()])

    def load_cluster(path: str) -> dict:
    """Load and validate a cluster file; resolve each job kind."""
    with open(path) as f:
        data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: expected a mapping")
    unknown = set(data) - TOP_KEYS
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: unknown key(s) {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    check_type(data.get("type"), path)
    jobs = data.get("jobs") or {}
    unknown = set(jobs) - set(JOB_KINDS)
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: unknown job kind(s) {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    limits = data.get("limits") or {}
    unknown = set(limits) - LIMIT_KEYS
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{path}: unknown limit(s) {', '.join(sorted(unknown))} "
            f"(cpus and mem are set per job kind, under jobs)"
        )

    resolved: dict = {k: data.get(k, DEFAULTS.get(k)) for k in ("type", "max_parallel", "output", "setup")}
    resolved["source"] = os.path.realpath(path)
    resolved["limits"] = dict(limits)
    resolved["jobs"] = {}
    base = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k in JOB_KEYS}
    for kind in JOB_KINDS:
        entry = jobs.get(kind) or {}
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: jobs.{kind} must be a mapping")
        unknown = set(entry) - JOB_KEYS
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: unknown key(s) in jobs.{kind}: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
        if kind == "check":
            job = {**base, **CHECK_DEFAULTS, **entry}
        else:
            job = {**base, **entry}
            if not (job.get("cpus") and job.get("mem")):
                raise ValueError(f"{path}: jobs.{kind} needs cpus and mem")
        job["mem_bytes"] = mem_bytes(job["mem"])
        job["extra"] = list(job.get("extra") or [])
        if isinstance(job.get("exclude"), str):
            job["exclude"] = [job["exclude"]]
        resolved["jobs"][kind] = job
    return resolved

    def limits_for(cluster: dict, kind: str, safety_margin: float = 1.0) -> str:
    """``--limits`` JSON line of the jobs of ``kind``: ``safety_margin`` of
    their memory, so a job does not size itself to its whole allocation."""
    job = cluster["jobs"][kind]
    limits = {"ram": int(job["mem_bytes"] * safety_margin), "threads": int(job["cpus"])}
    limits.update(cluster.get("limits") or {})
    return json.dumps(limits)

    def write_slurm(
    plan: dict,
    cluster: dict,
    slurm_dir: str,
    notify: Optional[str] = None,
    notify_level: str = "global",
) -> list[str]:
    """Write the SLURM files of ``plan`` to ``slurm_dir``; return their paths.

    ``jobs.txt`` (build jobs), ``build.sbatch`` (an array task runs one of
    them), ``publish.sbatch``, ``finish.sbatch`` (after every job: checks the
    registry when everything is done, then removes the lock files, writes
    ``progress.yaml``, mails it with ``notify``) and ``submit.sh``, which submits what ``apply --pending``
    lists, skipping the jobs still queued: safe to run again.

    With ``notify_level`` ``shard``, the build and publish jobs mail the end of
    their shard (a failed chunk, or the published shard).
    """
    os.makedirs(slurm_dir, exist_ok=True)
    build_dir = plan["build_dir"]
    definition = plan["definition"]
    apply = f"kmhelpers apply {shlex.quote(definition)} -o {shlex.quote(build_dir)}"
    output = os.path.join(build_dir, cluster["output"])
    single = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(output), "%x_%j.out")
    setup = (cluster.get("setup") or "").rstrip("\n")
    head = ["#!/usr/bin/env bash"]
    body_head = ["set -euo pipefail"] + ([setup] if setup else [])
    shard_mail = (
        f" --notify {shlex.quote(notify)} --notify-level shard --no-notify-final"
        if notify and notify_level == "shard"
        else ""
    )
    # a failed dependency cancels the job, so finish always runs
    no_wait = ["#SBATCH --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes"]

    build_jobs, publishes = [], {}
    for task in plan["tasks"].values():
        for job, steps in task["jobs"].items():
            if steps == [PUBLISH]:
                publishes[task["shard"]] = job
            else:
                build_jobs.append(job)
    name = os.path.basename(build_dir.rstrip("/"))
    finish_cmds = [
        "# Every job has ended: check the registry when nothing is pending,",
        "# remove the lock files once the build is done and checked,",
        "# write progress.yaml (and mail it), fail when the build is not done",
        f"PENDING=$({apply} --pending)",
        "CHECK=0",
        'if [ -z "$PENDING" ]; then',
        f"    kmhelpers manage -r {shlex.quote(build_dir)} check || CHECK=$?",
        "fi",
        'if [ -z "$PENDING" ] && [ "$CHECK" -eq 0 ]; then',
        f"    {apply} --cleanup || true",
        "fi",
        f"{apply} --status" + (f" --notify {shlex.quote(notify)}" if notify else ""),
        '[ -z "$PENDING" ] && [ "$CHECK" -eq 0 ]',
    ]

    files = {
        "jobs.txt": "\n".join(build_jobs) + ("\n" if build_jobs else ""),
        "build.sbatch": "\n".join(
            head
            + _sbatch_lines(cluster["jobs"]["build"], f"{name}_build", output)
            + body_head
            + [
                "# Array task i runs line OFFSET + i + 1 of the job list $1",
                'JOB=$(sed -n "$((${2:-0} + SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID + 1))p" "$1")',
                f'{apply} --task "$JOB"{shard_mail}',
            ]
        ),
        "publish.sbatch": "\n".join(
            head
            + _sbatch_lines(cluster["jobs"]["publish"], None, single)
            + no_wait
            + body_head
            + ["# $1: a publish job of the plan (<shard>_publish)", f'{apply} --task "$1"{shard_mail}']
        ),
        "finish.sbatch": "\n".join(
            head
            + _sbatch_lines(cluster["jobs"]["check"], f"{name}_finish", single)
            + no_wait
            + body_head
            + finish_cmds
        ),
        "submit.sh": _submit_script(apply, setup, build_dir, publishes, cluster),
    }
    # an older plan's check.sbatch is replaced by finish.sbatch
    old = os.path.join(slurm_dir, "check.sbatch")
    if os.path.exists(old):
        os.remove(old)
    written = []
    for file_name, text in files.items():
        path = os.path.join(slurm_dir, file_name)
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")
        if file_name.endswith((".sh", ".sbatch")):
            os.chmod(path, 0o755)
        written.append(path)
    return written

    runner

    pykmhelpers.pipeline.index_ops.runner

    Run a plan: the scripts plan wrote, job by job (kmhelpers apply).

    PlanRunner loads BUILD_DIR/assets/<session>/plan.yaml, refuses it when its inputs changed, and runs the selected jobs (see plan_file). Every step is checked before it runs, so a job can be run again after an interruption:

    • a task is done when its shard is registered and holds every sample of its chunks;
    • a chunk is done when its task is, or when its kmtricks run is complete;
    • before publishing, the registry must still be as plan saw it (expects), or as the publish step itself leaves it when it was interrupted.

    Each step it runs is recorded in a state file, and progress.yaml is rewritten after each one (see status). A published shard has its partition count recorded in the layout, so later sessions are planned with it. Once every job is done, cleanup removes the lock files no process holds.
